chunks: The bound of travel in which shortening (taqsir) of prayer and breaking the fast (iftar) are obligatory is eight parasangs.

If a man's travel is four parasangs and he does not intend to return the same day, he has the choice to complete the full prayer or shorten it. But if he intends to return the same day, shortening is obligatory upon him.
Whoever's travel is one of disobedience (sin), completing the full prayer and fast is obligatory upon him. The one who completes the full prayer while traveling is like the one who shortens at home.

Those upon whom completing the prayer and fast is obligatory during travel are: the muleteer, the camel driver, the ishtiqan — and he is the courier — the shepherd, and the sailor; for it is their occupation.
Also the hunter, if his hunting is for vanity or sport; but if his hunting is from what supports his family/dependents, shortening of prayer and fast is obligatory upon him.
It is not of piety for a man to fast voluntarily during his journey. It is not permissible for the one who breaks his fast during travel in the month of Ramadan to engage in sexual intercourse.

key_terms.البر: Birr — piety, righteousness; voluntary fasting while traveling is discouraged as it goes against this mercy
key_terms.البريد: Barid — the postal/courier system; professional couriers do not receive the taqsir concession
key_terms.التقصير: Taqsir — the shortening of obligatory prayers (from 4 to 2 rak'at) during travel
key_terms.التمام: Tamam — completion of the full prayer (not shortened), obligatory for certain travelers
key_terms.الحضر: Hadar — state of residence (as opposed to traveling)
key_terms.الفراسخ: Farsakh (parasang) — a unit of distance, approximately 5.5–6 km; eight farsakhs is the minimum travel distance for taqsir
key_terms.المعصية: Ma'siya — disobedience/sin; traveling for sinful purposes forfeits the concession of taqsir
key_terms.المكاري: Mukari — one who rents out pack animals; a professional traveler

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum travel distance for shortening prayers (taqsir) in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This text lays out the jurisprudential rules of the traveler's prayer (salat al-musafir) and fasting. The minimum distance for taqsir is eight parasangs (approximately 44 km), with detailed rules for those whose travel is their livelihood and for those traveling in sin. The ruling that voluntary fasting is discouraged in travel reflects a mercy provision in Islamic law, and the prohibition on intercourse for those who break their fast protects the sanctity of Ramadan observance.

en.bilal-muhammad: The bound of travel in which taqsir (shortening) is obligatory in the prayer and the iftar in the fast is eight parasangs.

So, if the man’s travel is four parasangs, and he did not want to return on the same day, then he has a choice whether to complete (the full prayer) if he wants or to shorten if he wants. If he intends to return on the same day, then taqsir is obligatory upon him.

Someone whose travel is one of disobedience (i.e. sin), then completion in the fast and prayer is [obligatory] upon him. The one who completes [his prayer] in travel is as one who shortens in residence.

Those upon whom completion in the prayer and the fast is obligatory in travel are: the pack-animal driver, the camel driver, the ishtiqan (?) – and he is the courier (?) – the shepherd, and the sailor, for it is their work.
Also, the companion of the hunt if his hunt is out of vanity or merriment. If his hunt was out of what he supports his dependents thereby, then taqsir is [obligatory] upon him in the fast and salat.

It is not of piety that the man fast a voluntary [fast] in his travel. It is not permissible for the one who breaks his fast in travel in the month of Ramadan to have sexual intercourse (i.e. during the day).
